# f5xc_active_service_policies (Resource)

namespace creates logical independent workspace within a tenant. Within a namespace contained objects should have unique names.<br><br>Object within a namespace can only refer to objects within the same namespace or shared namespace or ves-io/shared namespace<br><br>All monitoring is scoped by namespace<br><br>List within namespace lists objects within same namespace or shared namespace or ves-io/shared namespace<br><br>User roles can be scoped by namespace<br><br>The 'namespace' value of a namespace object itself is empty string

To get more information about f5xc_active_service_policies, refer:

- [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.f5.com/docs-v2/api/namespace)

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: Active Service Policies - Policy

resource "f5xc_service_policy" "policy_one" {
  name      = "example-active-service-policy-one-84vt1kz4"
  namespace = "default"

  server_choice = {
    any_server = true
  }

  rule_choice = {
    allow_all_requests = true
  }
}


resource "f5xc_active_service_policies" "example" {
  namespace = "default"

  service_policies = [
    {
      name      = f5xc_service_policy.policy_one.name
      namespace = f5xc_service_policy.policy_one.namespace
    }
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `namespace` (String) namespace This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ''

### Optional

- `service_policies` (Attributes List) service_policies Service Policies is a sequential engine where policies (and rules within the policy) are evaluated one after the other. It's important to define the correct order (policies evaluated from top to bottom in the list) for service policies, to get the intended result. For each request, its characteristics are evaluated based on the match criteria in each service policy starting at the top. If there is a match in the current policy, then the policy takes effect, and no more policies are evaluated. Otherwise, the next policy is evaluated. If all policies are evaluated and none match, then the request will be denied by default. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service_policies))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an `import` block to import this resource by ID.

> **Note:** Replace placeholder values (for example, `<namespace>`, `<name>`) with actual values.

#### Command-Line Import

Use the following `command` to import this resource from the command line:

```shell
terraform import f5xc_active_service_policies.example <namespace>
```

#### HCL Import Block

Use the following `hcl` block to import this resource during `plan` or `apply`:

```hcl
import {
	id = "<namespace>"
	to = "f5xc_active_service_policies.example"
}
```
